testName: IISER IAT Mock Test: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Reflection of light by spherical mirrors
questions.question: An object is placed at a distance of 20 cm in front of a convex mirror of focal length 20 cm. What is the position and nature of the image formed?
options: 10 cm in front of the mirror, real and inverted
10 cm behind the mirror, virtual and erect
20 cm behind the mirror, virtual and erect
questions.explanation: Using the mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. For a convex mirror, f is positive (+20 cm). Object distance u = -20 cm. Substituting: 1/v + 1/(-20) = 1/20 ⇒ 1/v = 1/20 + 1/20 = 2/20 = 1/10. Therefore, v = +10 cm. A positive image distance for a mirror indicates the image forms behind it, making it virtual and erect.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction
questions.question: A bird is flying at a height of 36 m exactly above the surface of a calm lake. A fish is swimming exactly 12 m vertically below the surface of the water. If the refractive index of water is 4/3, at what apparent distance does the bird appear to be from the fish?
questions.explanation: When viewing from a denser medium (water) into a rarer medium (air), objects appear farther away. The apparent height of the bird h' = h × μ = 36 × (4/3) = 48 m above the surface. The total apparent distance from the fish = real depth of fish + apparent height of bird = 12 m + 48 m = 60 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Total internal reflection
questions.question: A beam of light travels from a dense glass block of refractive index 1.5 into a surrounding pool of water with a refractive index of 1.33 (or 4/3). What is the sine of the critical angle for total internal reflection to occur at this interface?
questions.explanation: The critical angle C is given by sin C = μ_rarer / μ_denser. Substituting the values: μ_rarer = 4/3 (water) and μ_denser = 1.5 = 3/2 (glass). sin C = (4/3) / (3/2) = (4/3) × (2/3) = 8/9.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction at spherical surfaces and by lenses
questions.question: Two thin lenses are placed in close physical contact to form an optical combination. The first is a convex lens of power +12 D, and the second is a concave lens of power -2 D. What is the effective focal length of this lens combination?
questions.explanation: The equivalent power of thin lenses in contact is P_eq = P₁ + P₂. Here, P_eq = +12 D - 2 D = +10 D. The focal length is f = 1 / P_eq = 1/10 meters. Converting to centimeters, f = (1/10) × 100 cm = +10 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Optical instruments
questions.question: An astronomical telescope is configured in normal adjustment (with the final image formed at infinity). The focal length of the objective lens is 150 cm and the focal length of the eyepiece is 5 cm. What are the magnifying power and the total length of the telescope tube, respectively?
questions.explanation: For an astronomical telescope in normal adjustment, the magnifying power M = f_o / f_e = 150 / 5 = 30. The total length of the telescope tube is L = f_o + f_e = 150 + 5 = 155 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction through a prism
questions.question: A thin prism having a small refracting angle of 6° is made of glass with a refractive index of 1.5. If this prism is completely immersed in water (refractive index 4/3), what will be the minimum angle of deviation produced for a monochromatic ray of light?
questions.explanation: The deviation produced by a thin prism is δ = (μ_rel - 1)A. The relative refractive index μ_rel = μ_prism / μ_surrounding = 1.5 / (4/3) = (3/2) / (4/3) = 9/8. Substituting the values: δ = (9/8 - 1) × 6° = (1/8) × 6° = 6/8° = 0.75°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction at spherical surfaces and by lenses
questions.question: A solid glass sphere has a radius of 5 cm and a refractive index of 1.5. A tiny air bubble is trapped inside it at a distance of 2 cm from the geometric center. If the bubble is viewed along the diameter from the side closer to the bubble, how far from the spherical surface does it appear to be?
questions.explanation: Using the spherical refraction formula: μ₂/v - μ₁/u = (μ₂ - μ₁)/R. Light travels from glass (μ₁ = 1.5) to air (μ₂ = 1.0). The bubble is 2 cm from the center, so its distance from the near surface is u = -(5 - 2) = -3 cm. The center of curvature is on the opposite side of incident light, so R = -5 cm. Substituting: 1/v - 1.5/(-3) = (1 - 1.5)/(-5) ⇒ 1/v + 0.5 = 0.1 ⇒ 1/v = -0.4. Thus, v = -2.5 cm. It appears 2.5 cm from the surface.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction at spherical surfaces and by lenses
questions.question: A plano-convex lens is made of glass with a refractive index of 1.5. The radius of curvature of its convex surface is 20 cm. The flat (plane) surface of the lens is heavily silvered to act as a mirror. What is the effective focal length and the optical nature of the resulting system?
options: Concave mirror of focal length 20 cm
Convex mirror of focal length 20 cm
Concave mirror of focal length 10 cm
Convex mirror of focal length 10 cm
questions.explanation: A silvered lens acts as a mirror with equivalent power P_eq = 2P_L + P_M. Power of the lens P_L = (μ - 1)(1/R₁ - 1/R₂). Light enters the convex side (R₁ = 20) and hits the flat side (R₂ = ∞), so P_L = (1.5 - 1)(1/20 - 0) = 1/40 cm⁻¹. The flat silvered surface acts as a plane mirror, so P_M = 0. P_eq = 2(1/40) + 0 = 1/20 cm⁻¹. The effective focal length F = -1/P_eq = -20 cm. A negative focal length indicates a concave mirror.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Total internal reflection
questions.question: A very small point source of light is placed at a depth of √7 meters below the surface of a large tank of transparent liquid. The refractive index of the liquid is 4/3. Light from the source emerges into the air above forming a bright circular region on the surface. What is the total area of this illuminated circle?
questions.explanation: The radius R of the illuminated circle is R = h tan C, where C is the critical angle. sin C = 1/μ = 3/4. From a right triangle, if opposite is 3 and hypotenuse is 4, adjacent is √(4² - 3²) = √7. Therefore, tan C = 3/√7. The radius R = √7 × (3/√7) = 3 m. The area of the circle is πR² = π(3)² = 9π m².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction at spherical surfaces and by lenses
questions.question: In a displacement method experiment to find the focal length of a convex lens, the distance between the fixed object and the fixed screen is 100 cm. Two sharp images are obtained on the screen for two distinct positions of the lens. If the ratio of the heights of the two images is exactly 9 : 1, what is the physical distance separating the two positions of the lens?
questions.explanation: In the displacement method, the magnifications of the two images relate by m₁ m₂ = 1. The ratio of image heights I₁/I₂ = m₁/m₂ = 9. Since m₁ = 1/m₂, m₁² = 9 ⇒ m₁ = 3. Using m₁ = v₁/u₁ = 3 ⇒ v₁ = 3u₁. The total distance D = u₁ + v₁ = 100. Substituting: u₁ + 3u₁ = 100 ⇒ 4u₁ = 100 ⇒ u₁ = 25 cm, and v₁ = 75 cm. The separation between lens positions is x = v₁ - u₁ = 75 - 25 = 50 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Reflection of light by spherical mirrors
questions.question: A point object is moving steadily along the principal axis of a concave mirror of focal length 20 cm. It is moving towards the mirror with a constant speed of 10 m/s. What is the exact velocity of the image at the instant the object is exactly 30 cm away from the pole of the mirror?
questions.explanation: Image velocity v_i = -m² v_o. First, find magnification m = f / (f - u). For a concave mirror, f = -20 cm, u = -30 cm. m = -20 / (-20 - (-30)) = -20 / 10 = -2. v_i = -(-2)² × v_o = -4 × v_o. If the object moves towards the mirror (+10 m/s in standard coordinate space facing mirror), v_i = -4 × (+10) = -40 m/s. The negative sign implies the image moves opposite to the object, meaning it moves away from the mirror.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Optical instruments
questions.question: A compound microscope uses an objective lens with a focal length of 1.25 cm and an eyepiece with a focal length of 5 cm. A small object is placed at a distance of 1.5 cm from the objective lens. If the microscope is adjusted so that the final image is formed at infinity, what is the magnitude of its magnifying power?
questions.explanation: Total magnification M = m_o × m_e = (v_o / |u_o|) × (D / f_e). First, calculate v_o using the lens formula: 1/v_o - 1/(-1.5) = 1/1.25 ⇒ 1/v_o + 1/1.5 = 1/1.25 ⇒ 1/v_o = 1/1.25 - 1/1.5 = 4/5 - 2/3 = (12 - 10)/15 = 2/15 ⇒ v_o = 7.5 cm. m_o = 7.5 / 1.5 = 5. For the eyepiece at infinity, m_e = D / f_e = 25 / 5 = 5. Total M = 5 × 5 = 25.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction at spherical surfaces and by lenses
questions.question: A symmetric biconvex lens of focal length 20 cm in air is made of glass (μ_g = 1.5). The lens is physically cut strictly transverse to its principal axis (sliced vertically into two equal plano-convex halves). One of these newly formed plano-convex halves is then completely immersed in a transparent liquid of refractive index 1.6. What is the new focal length of this half-lens in the liquid?
questions.explanation: Step 1: Original lens 1/20 = (1.5 - 1)(2/R) ⇒ R = 20 cm. Step 2: Cutting vertically yields a plano-convex lens (R₁ = 20, R₂ = ∞). Its focal length in air is 1/f' = (1.5 - 1)(1/20 - 0) = 1/40 ⇒ f' = 40 cm. Step 3: Immersed in liquid (μ_l = 1.6), apply Lens Maker's formula: 1/f_liq = (μ_g/μ_l - 1)(1/R₁ - 1/R₂) = (1.5/1.6 - 1)(1/20) = (15/16 - 1) × 1/20 = (-1/16) × 1/20 = -1/320. Thus, f_liq = -320 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Reflection of light by spherical mirrors
questions.question: A convex mirror produces a virtual image that is exactly 1/4 the size of the real object. If the focal length of the convex mirror is 20 cm, what is the distance of the object from the pole of the mirror?
questions.explanation: Magnification formula in terms of f and u: m = f / (f - u). A convex mirror always forms virtual, erect, and diminished images for real objects, meaning m is positive. So, m = +1/4. Focal length f = +20 cm. Substituting: 1/4 = 20 / (20 - u) ⇒ 20 - u = 80 ⇒ u = 20 - 80 = -60 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction at spherical surfaces and by lenses
questions.question: Two thin lenses of focal lengths +10 cm and -20 cm are mounted coaxially and separated by a distance of 5 cm. A wide beam of light parallel to the principal axis falls entirely on the first lens (the convex one). Where will the final image be formed by this combination?
questions.explanation: Lens 1 (+10 cm): Object at infinity forms an image at its focus, v₁ = +10 cm. Lens 2 (-20 cm): This image acts as a virtual object. It is separated by 5 cm, so u₂ = +(10 - 5) = +5 cm. Applying the lens formula for Lens 2: 1/v₂ - 1/(+5) = 1/(-20) ⇒ 1/v₂ = 1/5 - 1/20 = 4/20 - 1/20 = 3/20. Thus, v₂ = +20/3 ≈ +6.67 cm. A positive sign means the final image is formed behind the second lens.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Reflection of light by spherical mirrors
questions.question: A short linear object of length L₀ lies strictly along the principal axis of a concave mirror of focal length f. The center of the object is at a distance u from the pole of the mirror. Assuming L₀ is very small compared to u, what is the approximate length of the image formed?
questions.explanation: For a short object placed longitudinally along the principal axis, the longitudinal magnification m_L is equal to the derivative dv/du, which is strictly -m², where m is the transverse magnification. Length of image L_i = |m_L| × L₀ = m² L₀. Transverse magnification m = f / (f - u). Squaring this gives m² = (f / (f - u))² = (f / (u - f))². Final image length is L₀ (f / (u - f))².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Total internal reflection
questions.question: A ray of monochromatic light is incident at an angle θ on one of the refracting faces of a glass prism with a refracting angle A = 60° and a refractive index μ = √2. The refracted ray travels through the prism and emerges from the second face such that it just perfectly grazes the surface (grazing emergence). What is the exact value of the incident angle θ?
questions.explanation: Grazing emergence means angle e = 90°, so the angle of refraction at the second face r₂ equals the critical angle C. sin r₂ = sin C = 1/μ = 1/√2 ⇒ r₂ = 45°. For a prism, A = r₁ + r₂ ⇒ 60° = r₁ + 45° ⇒ r₁ = 15°. Apply Snell's law at the first face: sin θ = μ sin r₁ = √2 sin(15°). Using the identity sin(45-30), sin 15° = (√3-1)/(2√2). Substitute to get sin θ = √2 × (√3-1)/(2√2) = (√3-1)/2. Therefore, θ = sin⁻¹((√3-1)/2).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Reflection of light by spherical mirrors
questions.question: A convex lens of focal length 20 cm is placed 10 cm directly in front of a flat plane mirror, with its principal axis perpendicular to the mirror. A point object is placed on the principal axis at a distance of 30 cm in front of the lens (on the side opposite the mirror). After the light passes through the lens, reflects off the mirror, and passes back through the lens again, where is the final image formed?
options: 13.33 cm in front of the lens
20 cm in front of the lens
40 cm in front of the lens
questions.explanation: First pass (Lens): u = -30 cm, f = 20 cm. 1/v₁ - 1/(-30) = 1/20 ⇒ v₁ = +60 cm (converging 60 cm behind lens). Reflection (Mirror): Mirror is 10 cm behind lens, so the virtual object is u_m = +50 cm. It forms a real image at v_m = -50 cm (50 cm in front of mirror, which is 40 cm in front of the lens). Light now travels backwards. Second pass (Lens): Rays from the mirror aim at a point 40 cm in front of the lens. They hit the lens first. Since they are converging towards -40 cm (in original coordinates), it's a virtual object for the backward pass. Let backward direction be positive: u₂ = +40 cm. f = +20 cm. 1/v₂ - 1/(+40) = 1/20 ⇒ 1/v₂ = 1/20 + 1/40 = 3/40. v₂ = +40/3 = 13.33 cm in the backward direction (in front of the lens).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction at spherical surfaces and by lenses
questions.question: A solid glass sphere has a refractive index of 1.5 and a radius of 10 cm. A point object is placed in the air exactly 20 cm away from the geometric center of the sphere, resting on an extended diametrical axis. After light from the object refracts through both the front and back surfaces of the sphere, where is the final image formed?
options: 20 cm from the second surface, outside the sphere
50 cm from the second surface, outside the sphere
30 cm from the first surface, inside the sphere
40 cm from the geometric center, outside the sphere
questions.explanation: First surface: u₁ = -10 cm (20 cm from center - 10 cm radius). 1.5/v₁ - 1/(-10) = (1.5 - 1)/10 ⇒ 1.5/v₁ + 0.1 = 0.05 ⇒ 1.5/v₁ = -0.05 ⇒ v₁ = -30 cm (Virtual image 30 cm left of first surface). Second surface: Object distance u₂ = -(30 + 20) = -50 cm (it is 50 cm from the second surface). Light goes from glass (1.5) to air (1). Radius R₂ = -10 cm. 1/v₂ - 1.5/(-50) = (1 - 1.5)/(-10) = 0.05. 1/v₂ + 0.03 = 0.05 ⇒ 1/v₂ = 0.02 = 1/50 ⇒ v₂ = +50 cm. The final image is 50 cm to the right of the second surface.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Optical instruments
questions.question: An achromatic optical doublet is manufactured by combining two thin lenses in contact: a convex lens made of crown glass and a concave lens made of flint glass. The crown glass lens has a focal length of 20 cm and a dispersive power of 0.03. The flint glass lens has a dispersive power of 0.05. What is the effective focal length of the final achromatic combination?
questions.explanation: The condition for an achromatic doublet is ω₁/f₁ + ω₂/f₂ = 0. Substituting the given values: 0.03/20 + 0.05/f₂ = 0 ⇒ 0.05/f₂ = -0.03/20 ⇒ f₂ = - (0.05 × 20) / 0.03 = -1 / 0.03 = -100/3 cm. To find the effective focal length F of the combination: 1/F = 1/f₁ + 1/f₂ = 1/20 - 3/100 = 5/100 - 3/100 = 2/100 = 1/50. Therefore, F = +50.0 cm.
